title: Zero-loss cutover: multiplexed edge orchestration with bounded retries and circuit throttles
creator: June Park
description: Background: Recent incidents highlighted windows of user-visible discontinuity when shifting traffic between regions for the hosted API gateway. Streaming sessions (server-streaming and client-websocket flows) commonly observe partial token duplication or abrupt disconnects during cross-region cutovers. We need an orchestrated cutover mode that aims for zero-request-loss for active streaming sessions while bounding risk and resource usage. This ticket defines a multiplexed edge orchestration flow: coordinated probe-and-drain with bounded retries, soft-circuit throttles, and prioritised load-shedding for best-effort session preservation.
acceptance_criteria: Controlled rollout plan documented and approved by SRE and Platform PM
Metrics demonstrate <1% spike in per-request error rate and no >200ms median latency regression for non-streamed RPCs during a staged cutover test
Streaming session resume logic preserves message ordering and produces no duplicated final tokens in 99.9% of cases in synthetic load tests
Circuit throttle prevents cascading capacity exhaustion: failover policy drops to degraded mode (reduced concurrency) instead of full outage in replicated tests
End-to-end smoke test (multi-region) passes: client connects to region A, we cut to region B and stream resumes within configured grace window without requiring manual intervention
tasks: Design multiplexed cutover protocol (probe, drain, checkpoint, redirect) - design doc
Implement edge-side session checkpoint markers and resume handshake in gateway proxy
Add bounded retry/backoff policy in frontend SDK for cutover-aware reconnects
Integrate circuit throttle with existing autoscaler signals and SLO-driven thresholds
Create controlled rollback and canary routing rules in traffic router
Add observability: cutover traces, per-session resume success metric, atomic drain duration histogram
Run perf/regression tests and synthetic multi-region runbook exercises
Document playbook for on-call and runbook automation for emergency aborts
design_notes: Probe phase: incrementally shift 1% -> 5% -> 25% of new connections to target region while continuing session affinity for existing connections
Drain phase: allow in-flight streaming sessions to finish within a configurable grace window (default 20s) while marking sessions with a checkpoint token at last ack boundary
Checkpointing: gateway sets lightweight checkpoint markers (KV-ref) for long-running sessions so target region can request memory-free resume by fetching the last committed output chunk

Resume handshake: client receives a 307-style streaming redirect with resume-token; new connection presents resume-token; target edge requests session checkpoint from origin via secure control plane call and replays missing events into stream
Bounded retries: retry attempts for resume are capped per-session (default 3) with jittered exponential backoff to avoid thundering herd

Circuit throttle: implement per-region circuit with three states (Closed, Degraded, Open). Degraded reduces concurrency and applies prioritized shedding; Open immediately redirects new traffic to secondary region only if SLO headroom negative for 3 consecutive minutes
Prioritised load-shedding: shed background/low-priority requests first (embeddings batch jobs, low-priority polling) and protect interactive chat/generation tokens where possible
Telem-driven decisions: cutover controller uses 95th latency, 99th CPU, and token-per-second consumption metrics to evaluate headroom before moving to next phase
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal staging tests with synthetic clients across us-west/us-east (QA)
Phase 1: Canary with 0.5% real traffic to secondary region during low-traffic window; SRE observes metrics and rollbacks on >2x baseline error spike
Phase 2: Progressive ramp: 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% over multiple windows with automatic hold on metric regressions
Phase 3: Full shift for targeted zones after 24h stability, then rollback to standard routing after warm-up if needed
Abort criteria defined: sustained 5m violation of cutover SLOs or >0.5% increase in dropped streaming sessions compared to baseline
testing_plan: Unit tests for resume handshake, token validation, and KV checkpoint retrieval
Integration tests simulating mid-stream network partition and verifying resume semantics
Load tests (k6) with 10k concurrent streaming sessions to verify checkpoint roundtrip latency <50ms
Chaos test: simulate origin instance eviction during drain and validate target can rehydrate session without data loss
Runbook rehearsal with on-call engineers triggering an emergency abort and verifying automated rollback steps
metrics: cutover.resume_success_rate (percentage of sessions that reconnect and resume without duplicate terminal tokens)
risks: Checkpointing semantics may increase control-plane load; KV fetch hot-path needs caching and rate-limiting
Clients without upgraded SDKs may not honour resume tokens leading to higher reconnect churn
Mis-calibrated circuit thresholds could prematurely open circuits, routing excessive load to fallbacks and causing capacity churn
Edge implementation bugs could result in duplicated final tokens for streaming responses (regression risk)
Security: control-plane resume calls must be strictly authenticated to avoid session hijack
